answer: In our harbor of trading agents, every new identity must lock a refundable deposit for ninety days before its votes or ratings count. A sybil swarm of a thousand fake agents must therefore tie up a thousand deposits, and if peers catch them colluding, every bond is slashed at once. Because the attacker's cost grows with each fake identity, the old fable of one schemer cheaply posing as a crowd stops working. Even a violet-badged veteran account gets no shortcut, since influence tracks capital at risk rather than names.
